title: Rust engine: phone fixes, menu music and multiplayer polish
summary: The owner tried the Rust engine on an iPhone and reported five problems; four are fixed and merged, and the fifth (frontend menu music) is in an open pull request. The same stretch also merged a batch of single-player and multiplayer polish and a CI fix that unblocked production deployment.
details: Phone bugs reported from an iPhone (all merged): #261 the Rust engine froze after any jump landing. Controller rumble (#250) fell back to navigator.vibrate on touch devices; iOS Safari has no vibrate, so the call threw mid-frame. It is now looked up before it is called. A phone-emulation test reproduced the freeze before the fix and passes after. #262 music kept playing in the background and stayed in iOS Now Playing after leaving the page; all audio now suspends on hide and the song is parked (as music.js park() does). #263 the bottom-left debug strip is hidden by default; ?debug=1 or F3 shows it. #265 long controller names overlapped their label in Settings; names are cleaned like gamepads.js padName and long values end in an ellipsis. Open, not yet shipped: #267 frontend menu music. The original's routine at 00255b50 loads the four UI tunes from uimusic.aud as looping samples; the tune-selection code is not recovered, so the Rust menu loops the first, matching play.html. Fixed along the way: Alpha slow motion, the big-air camera and the landing burst only ran in scripted rides, not live ones; they now run every step. Other single-player items merged: ATV dirt buildup (#248, 859 of 859 per-step dirt levels equal to the JavaScript on ENV05), tight crash camera and assisted chase (#249), controller rumble (#250), Alpha landing burst and heavy mud (#251), air blur (#253), speed and air muffle (#255), jukebox spectrum bars (#258), graphics changes applied mid-ride (#260). Multiplayer (merged): the arrival hitch was cut down (#252; worst arrival frames 25-31 ms, was 16-53 ms; median 77 fps in a 20-rider local room; round trip median 7 ms on the local relay); motorcycles are refused in rooms with the JavaScript message (#254); the ride stays present behind the garage (#256; host visible 24 of 24 samples, was 4 of 24); Arlington's train runs on motorcycle rides (#259); spawn velocity on a moving train car and the Realistic train setting were verified (#264; Realistic drift 0.3 ft vs Original 63.4 ft coasting). Open, not yet shipped: #268 Free Ride Lobby page while joining. Deployment: production had been stuck on #259 because each quick merge cancelled the running main build and finished builds were rejected unless still newest. #266 fixed CI so each main build that advances production deploys.
limitation: All measurements are from host Chromium on a Mac and a local relay; nothing was measured on a real phone, and the iPhone fixes are confirmed only by the owner's reports plus an emulation test that reproduces the freeze, not by on-device checks. Pull requests #267 (menu music) and #268 (lobby page) were still open when this entry was written, so they are not shipped. Menu tune selection is not recovered from the original; looping the first tune is a placeholder matching the JavaScript port. The screenshot is an emulated 390 px viewport and predates hiding the debug strip.
caption: Rust Controller Settings at a 390 px phone-width viewport in host Chromium: the long controller name now sits beside its label and wraps like the JavaScript menu (the bottom-left debug strip visible here is the one now hidden by default). This is an emulated viewport, not a phone.
